One posterior edge probability as a p x p matrix

Source: R/edge_probs.R
edge_prob_matrix.Rd

Extracts a single quantity from edge_probs() for one group or one pair of groups, as a symmetric matrix.

Usage

edge_prob_matrix(
  fit,
  quantity = c("p_struct", "p_cut", "mean_weight", "mean", "sd", "p_sign", "p_exceed",
    "p_union", "p_up", "p_down", "mcse_struct", "mcse_cut", "mcse_exceed", "mcse_union",
    "mean_shrinkage", "p_shrinkage", "mcse_shrinkage"),
  group = NULL,
  pair = NULL,
  c = NULL,
  scale = c("precision", "pcor"),
  chain = NULL
)

Arguments

fit

A multiggm_fit or multiggm_fit_list.

quantity

One of the columns of edge_probs() without the threshold suffix: "p_struct", "p_cut", "mean_weight", "mean", "sd", "p_sign", "p_exceed", "p_union", "p_up", "p_down", "mcse_struct", "mcse_cut", "mcse_exceed" or "mcse_union".

group

A single group, for per-group quantities.

pair

Two groups c(s, t), for differential quantities. For "mean", "p_up" and "p_down" the direction follows the order (\(D = x_s - x_t\)).

c

A single threshold, required for the quantities with a threshold ("p_exceed", "p_union", "p_up", "p_down", "mcse_exceed", "mcse_union").

scale

"precision" (default) or "pcor": the scale of mean, sd, p_exceed_*, p_union_* and p_sign.

chain

NULL (default) pools all chains; an integer selects chains.

Value

A symmetric p x p matrix with zero diagonal.

See also

edge_probs(), select_edges()

Examples

sim <- simulate_multiggm(K = 2, p = 6, n = 60, seed = 1)
fit <- multiggm_mcmc(data_list = sim$data_list, burnin = 100, nsave = 100)
edge_prob_matrix(fit, "p_union", pair = c(1, 2), c = 0.05)
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4] [,5] [,6]
#> [1,] 0.00 0.50 0.79 0.15 0.32 0.13
#> [2,] 0.50 0.00 1.00 0.75 0.27 0.90
#> [3,] 0.79 1.00 0.00 0.31 0.98 0.40
#> [4,] 0.15 0.75 0.31 0.00 1.00 0.90
#> [5,] 0.32 0.27 0.98 1.00 0.00 1.00
#> [6,] 0.13 0.90 0.40 0.90 1.00 0.00
